newsitem.title: UK: BA urges approval of American pact.
newsitem.headline: BA urges approval of American pact.

text.p: British Airways Plc (BA) said on Wednesday that the launch of the rival Star Alliance grouping of airlines should improve its own prospects of approval for its alliance with American Airlines.

BA and American both urged UK and U.S. regulators to clear their pact in the light of Star. BA said the Star Alliance was "final proof that airline alliances are now a major feature of the air transport market".
Earlier Deutsche Lufthansa AG and United Airlines formally branded their grouping of airlines which currently include SAS, Air Canada, Thai International Airways Ltd and Varig.
"If ever proof was needed that commercial aviation is moving towards global alliance then today's Star announcement is the ultimate proof," said BA chief executive Bob Ayling.

BA and American said when they announced their own alliance on June 11 last year that it was in response to the growth of rival alliances, including the United-Lufthansa-SAS axis which was already in place.
But the BA-American deal has come under fierce attack from rival airlines, including United, and is still enmeshed in a complex web of regulatory processes in the U.S. and Europe.

"British Airways and American are prevented from competing on equal terms with this (Star) and other alliances and from offering consumers the wider choice and better quality of service which our alliance would provide," Ayling said on Wednesday.

American's chairman Robert Crandall said in a separate statement: "The good news is that the unveiling of the Star Alliance, which is far larger than the proposed American/BA alliance, will presumably end United Airlines' hypocritical opposition to our planned alliance."
